description: Black-box agent-readiness checks that any HTTP client can reproduce against a public documentation site. Every check is binary or a pass rate across the sampled pages.

scoring.formula: round(100 * sum(w_c * s_c) / sum(w_c)) over applicable categories; s_c = weighted mean of applicable scored check values
scoring.binaryStatus: pass when value == 1; fail when value == 0
scoring.notApplicable: a not-applicable check leaves its category mean; a category with no applicable scored checks leaves the weight sum

probes.llmsTxt: if root path != '/': ['<root>llms.txt', '/llms.txt'] else ['/llms.txt']; llms-full only beside the llms.txt hit, else '/llms-full.txt'

sampling.method: k = floor(n/10); U[i*k], i=0..9; plus docs root
sampling.fallback: breadth-first same-site links from the docs root in document order, extended by links from already-sampled pages

checks.rule: The llms.txt location returns 200 with a text/* media type that is not text/html, and the decoded body, after removing the BOM and leading whitespace, starts with '# '.
checks.notApplicableWhen: the probe was reached with the request budget exhausted (reason: budget)

checks.rule: llms-full.txt returns 200 with a text/* media type that is not text/html, and more than 1024 bytes. Only the first 2048 bytes are read.
checks.notApplicableWhen: the probe was reached with the request budget exhausted (reason: budget)

checks.rule: Sitemap candidates, in order and de-duplicated: robots.txt Sitemap lines on the same site, then probes.sitemapPaths at the origin, then <root>sitemap.xml; at most 3 are fetched. At least one fetched sitemap parses with root <urlset> or <sitemapindex> and yields at least one <loc> under the docs root.
checks.notApplicableWhen: the probe was reached with the request budget exhausted (reason: budget)

checks.rule: For each of GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot, robots.txt allows the docs root path. A missing or 4xx robots.txt allows all. Reported, not scored.

Probe URLs share one allocation of 3 (the number of well-known paths). If llms.txt contains an absolute http(s) URL whose host starts with 'mcp.' or whose path has a segment 'mcp', that URL is fetched first with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream and takes one slot; the remaining slots go to the well-known paths in order. Passes on any of: (a) a well-known probe returns 200, a JSON media type and a JSON object; (b) the llms.txt MCP URL is plausibly an endpoint: status 400, 405 or 406, or a 2xx response with a JSON or text/event-stream media type, or any 2xx non-HTML response at a path whose last segment is 'mcp' (a 200 HTML page is not an endpoint); (c) the docs root HTML has <link rel="mcp"> or the response has a Link header with rel="mcp".
checks.notApplicableWhen: a probe was skipped for budget and nothing else passed (reason: budget)

checks.rule: Exactly one <link rel=canonical>, and its href resolved against the final URL equals the final URL after normalization.
<title> text is non-empty and <meta name=description> content is non-empty.

Any of: dateModified on the page's JSON-LD node (see parity.description for node selection) at any depth, or on any JSON-LD node when the page has no node of a page type in probes.jsonLdPageTypes; a non-empty <meta property="article:modified_time">; or a <time> element whose own, parent's or grandparent's text matches /\b(last\s+)?(updated|modified|edited)\b/i.
The whole document contains exactly one <h1>.

Within the main content root, walking h1-h6 in document order, no heading is more than one level deeper than the previous heading. Upward jumps are allowed and the first heading may be any level. A page with fewer than 2 headings passes.
At least one <script type="application/ld+json">; every such script parses as JSON, and every top-level object, or every node of its @graph, has a non-empty @type.

Main content root text is at least 200 characters in the raw HTML, without executing JavaScript. The main content root is the first <main>, else the first <article>, else the first [role=main], else <body> without header, nav, footer and aside; script, style, noscript, template and svg are removed first.

On the probe page, the variants are tried in order and the first valid one passes. Markdown: 200, media type text/markdown, text/x-markdown or text/plain (text/plain only for variants (1) and (2)), body not starting with '<'. JSON: 200, application/json or *+json, body parses to an object. Feeds never count: media types application/rss+xml, application/atom+xml and application/feed+json, and URLs whose path ends in 'feed.json' or 'feed'. Variants: (1) the first HTML <link rel=alternate> or HTTP Link alternate of type text/markdown or application/json whose target is not llms.txt, llms-full.txt or a feed and is on the same site (a declared alternate on another host is recorded and not fetched, and the check fails if nothing else passes); (2) <url>.md, or <url>index.md when the path ends with '/'; (3) the same URL with Accept: text/markdown, application/json;q=0.9 (plain content negotiation; a text/markdown, text/x-markdown or JSON response counts); (4) <url>?format=json with Accept: application/json.
checks.notApplicableWhen: every variant was skipped for budget (reason: budget)

checks.rule: The sampled page reached a final status of 200 with at most 2 redirects. Errors and offsite redirects fail.

Any of: a JSON-LD node with @type Organization at any depth (including publisher or author); or a <footer> or [role=contentinfo] containing at least one <a href> and text matching /©|\(c\)|copyright/i.

Any <a href> matching github.com/<owner>/<repo>/(edit|blob|tree)/, gitlab.com/.+/-/(edit|blob)/ or bitbucket.org/.+/src/, or page text matching /edit (this )?page|suggest (an )?edit|improve this (page|doc)|report an issue|was this (page )?helpful|give feedback/i.

The alternate title (Markdown: frontmatter title, else the first '# ' heading; JSON: top-level title, then headline, then name, where a JSON-LD shaped object with @graph or @type uses the page node selected as in parity.description), normalized by NFKC, lower-case, collapsed whitespace and stripped punctuation, equals the normalized first <h1>, or the normalized <title> starts with it.

On pages that have both a meta description and a JSON-LD description, the normalized values are equal. The JSON-LD description is taken from the page node: among top-level nodes (including @graph members) of a type in probes.jsonLdPageTypes, the node whose url or @id (ignoring the fragment) equals the page URL, else the first node of the earliest type in that list (in document order); a site-level node (for example WebSite or Organization) is used only when the page has no node of a page type.
